title: Most Drivers Cannot Pass This Motorcycle Driving Test
summary: Explore motorcycle awareness through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Think beyond the handlebars.
Test your road awareness.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of motorcycle awareness. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. Not a licensing test or a substitute for professional rider training and local road rules.

motorbike-s1q1.question: What connects the engine’s drive to the rear wheel on a chain-driven motorcycle?

answers.a3: The front brake hose

motorbike-s1q2.question: What does the clutch do on a conventional manual motorcycle?

answers.a1: Connects and disconnects engine drive from the transmission
answers.a3: Controls only the headlight

motorbike-s1q3.question: What is the throttle used to control?

answers.a3: Tyre inflation directly

motorbike-s1q4.question: What do suspension springs and dampers help manage?

answers.a2: Wheel movement and the motorcycle’s response to the road
answers.a3: The shape of the licence plate

motorbike-s1q5.question: What is the main job of the front and rear brakes?

answers.a3: Reduce speed through controlled braking force

motorbike-s1q6.question: What does a motorcycle’s transmission provide?

answers.a1: Automatic protection from all road hazards
answers.a3: An unlimited fuel supply
answers.a4: Different gear ratios between engine and driven wheel

motorbike-s1q7.question: Why does a motorcycle need functioning lights?

answers.a2: To help the rider see and be seen as required
answers.a3: To replace observation
answers.a4: To guarantee every other road user notices it

motorbike-s2q1.question: Where should a rider find the correct tyre pressure for a motorcycle and load?

answers.a1: The manufacturer’s guidance for that motorcycle
answers.a2: The number on an unrelated bicycle
answers.a3: A pressure chosen from the tyre’s colour
answers.a4: A guess based only on the weather

motorbike-s2q2.question: A tyre has visible damage. What is appropriate before riding?

answers.a1: Ignore it if the engine starts
answers.a3: Have its safety assessed and address the defect

motorbike-s2q3.question: A brake control feels unexpectedly different. What should the rider do?

answers.a1: Ride faster to test it in traffic
answers.a2: Investigate and resolve the issue before relying on it
answers.a3: Assume all changes are harmless

motorbike-s2q4.question: Why check the drive chain according to the manufacturer’s instructions?

answers.a1: Every chain has the same adjustment
answers.a3: Its condition and adjustment affect safe operation

motorbike-s2q5.question: What should be checked about a mirror before setting off?

answers.a2: It is secure and adjusted for useful rearward visibility
answers.a3: It shows only the rider’s face

motorbike-s2q6.question: A warning symbol appears and its meaning is unfamiliar. Where should it be checked?

answers.a1: The motorcycle’s owner manual or qualified support
answers.a2: A guess from the symbol’s colour alone
answers.a3: The length of the journey

motorbike-s2q7.question: Why check for fluid leaks before a ride?

answers.a1: Only the smell of fuel matters
answers.a3: Every leak is a normal way to reduce weight
answers.a4: They may indicate a fault and can affect safety

motorbike-s3q1.question: Why can loose gravel reduce a motorcycle tyre’s grip?

answers.a3: It can move between the tyre and road surface
answers.a4: It eliminates the need to brake

motorbike-s3q2.question: What can painted road markings become when wet?

answers.a3: A replacement for road signs

motorbike-s3q3.question: Why can abrupt control inputs be risky when grip is limited?

answers.a1: They can demand more traction than is available
answers.a3: They remove the motorcycle’s mass

motorbike-s3q4.question: What happens to the available grip when tyres are also providing cornering force?

answers.a3: Road condition no longer matters
answers.a4: Braking and turning share the available traction

motorbike-s3q5.question: Why should tyre condition matter in wet weather?

answers.a1: All worn tyres grip better in rain
answers.a2: Tread and condition influence water clearance and grip
answers.a3: Only the motorcycle’s colour matters

motorbike-s3q6.question: A shaded section of road may be icy. What is the sound response?

answers.a2: Ignore the surface if the sky is clear
answers.a3: Recognise the reduced-grip risk and adapt the plan
answers.a4: Use sudden steering to test the surface

motorbike-s3q7.question: Why should a rider allow more margin on an unfamiliar surface?

answers.a1: The available grip and hazards may be uncertain
answers.a3: A familiar speed is safe on every surface
answers.a4: Unfamiliar roads always have more grip

motorbike-s4q1.question: What is stopping distance made up of?

answers.a1: Only the length of the motorcycle
answers.a2: Distance travelled while reacting plus distance travelled while braking
answers.a3: Only the distance after reaching a stop
answers.a4: Only the gap to the nearest junction

motorbike-s4q2.question: At a higher speed with the same reaction time, what happens to reaction distance?

answers.a3: It depends only on helmet colour

motorbike-s4q3.question: Why leave a suitable following gap?

answers.a2: To allow time and space to respond
answers.a3: To replace checking the road ahead
answers.a4: To guarantee the vehicle ahead never brakes

motorbike-s4q4.question: What does an anti-lock braking system help prevent during braking?

answers.a1: Wheel lock under conditions within its operating capability
answers.a2: Every possible skid in every situation
answers.a3: All collisions regardless of speed

motorbike-s4q5.question: Why does an anti-lock braking system not justify riding too close?

answers.a1: It makes stopping distance always zero
answers.a2: It cannot remove reaction time or the need for space
answers.a3: It controls all other vehicles
answers.a4: It guarantees the road is dry

motorbike-s4q6.question: A downhill gradient can affect stopping. What should a rider do?

answers.a1: Ignore the gradient if travelling in a straight line
answers.a2: Assume downhill stopping is always shorter
answers.a3: Allow for the conditions and the motorcycle’s limitations
answers.a4: Use a fixed gap in every situation

motorbike-s4q7.question: Why should braking technique follow motorcycle-specific training?

answers.a2: Training matters only at walking speed
answers.a3: One technique removes every hazard
answers.a4: Design, loading and conditions affect the response

motorbike-s5q1.question: Why assess a bend before entering it?

answers.a1: To avoid looking through the bend
answers.a2: To choose speed from the road’s name
answers.a3: To judge the visible path, conditions and appropriate speed
answers.a4: To guarantee there are no unseen hazards

motorbike-s5q2.question: A bend tightens beyond the visible section. What was uncertain?

answers.a1: Only the colour of the road
answers.a3: The number of letters on a sign
answers.a4: The full path and required turning demand

motorbike-s5q3.question: Why should a rider avoid fixing their gaze only on one nearby obstacle?

answers.a3: It can reduce awareness of the intended path and other hazards
answers.a4: It removes the need to choose a path

motorbike-s5q4.question: What can an unexpected patch of gravel inside a bend change?

answers.a3: The engine’s number of cylinders
answers.a4: The legal identity of the motorcycle

motorbike-s5q5.question: Why is available sight distance relevant to speed selection?

answers.a1: The rider needs space to respond within what can be seen
answers.a2: Sight distance matters only when stationary
answers.a3: Higher speed always increases visible distance
answers.a4: A hidden road is always clear

motorbike-s5q6.question: What is a useful general principle for control inputs through a bend?

answers.a1: They should be copied from a different vehicle without training
answers.a3: They should ignore the surface
answers.a4: They should be smooth and appropriate to the available grip

motorbike-s5q7.question: Why must a planned path through a bend stay adaptable?

answers.a1: The initial view contains every future detail
answers.a2: Other road users or surface conditions may change the situation
answers.a3: A plan guarantees nobody else appears

motorbike-s6q1.question: A parked vehicle has a person inside near traffic. What possible hazard should a rider anticipate?

answers.a3: The absence of any need to observe
answers.a4: A door opening or the vehicle moving

motorbike-s6q2.question: Why can a motorcycle be difficult for another driver to notice?

answers.a2: Its smaller visual profile can be less conspicuous
answers.a3: Motorcycles are invisible by definition

motorbike-s6q3.question: A large vehicle blocks the view of a junction. What should that suggest?

answers.a2: There may be hazards hidden beyond it
answers.a3: Visibility no longer affects decisions

motorbike-s6q4.question: Why check blind spots using the appropriate trained observation method?

answers.a1: Only the road behind can matter
answers.a2: A signal creates a guaranteed gap
answers.a3: Mirrors may not show every relevant area
answers.a4: Mirrors always show the complete surroundings

motorbike-s6q5.question: A pedestrian looks away from traffic near the road edge. What is the safer assumption?

answers.a1: They have seen every approaching vehicle
answers.a3: They may not have noticed the motorcycle

motorbike-s6q6.question: Why should a rider be cautious about assuming eye contact proves they were seen?

answers.a3: Recognition never matters
answers.a4: Another road user may look in that direction without recognising the hazard

motorbike-s6q7.question: A gap is closing as another vehicle approaches. What should guide the decision?

answers.a1: The assumption the other vehicle will stop
answers.a3: Only the size of the original gap
answers.a4: Current speed, distance and a safe margin

motorbike-s7q1.question: Why does carrying a passenger affect motorcycle handling?

answers.a2: It removes the effect of gravity
answers.a3: It changes mass and weight distribution

motorbike-s7q2.question: What should determine whether a motorcycle can carry a passenger?

answers.a2: The length of the journey alone
answers.a3: Only whether there is room on the fuel tank
answers.a4: Its design, equipment, manufacturer guidance and applicable rules

motorbike-s7q3.question: Why should a passenger receive a clear briefing before the ride?

answers.a1: Their movements and actions can affect the ride
answers.a2: It makes the rider’s training unnecessary
answers.a3: It guarantees no unexpected events

answers.a1: According only to the largest available bag
answers.a3: Where it blocks controls
answers.a4: Securely and within the motorcycle’s loading guidance

motorbike-s7q5.question: Why does a helmet need to fit properly?

answers.a1: A loose fit guarantees ventilation without risk
answers.a3: Fit is important to its protective function

motorbike-s7q6.question: A rider feels very tired before a journey. What is appropriate?

answers.a2: Use confidence as a substitute for rest
answers.a3: Ride faster to finish sooner
answers.a4: Assume fatigue affects only car drivers

motorbike-s7q7.question: A medicine may cause drowsiness. What should the rider check?

answers.a2: The medicine’s advice and appropriate professional guidance before riding
answers.a3: Whether the journey is familiar

answers.a1: The temperature at which water freezes
answers.a3: The mass of an object
answers.a4: A force that opposes relative motion between contacting surfaces

motorbike-s8q2.question: What does a lever turn around?

answers.a3: A fuel injector

motorbike-s8q3.question: Two meshed external gears turn together. If one turns clockwise, how does the other turn?

answers.a3: Anticlockwise

motorbike-s8q4.question: What does a pulley change in a simple fixed-pulley system?

answers.a1: The direction of the applied force
answers.a3: The force of gravity itself
Mass multiplied by volume

motorbike-s8q6.question: What does a spring generally do when compressed within its elastic range?

answers.a3: Stores energy and tends to return to its original shape

motorbike-s8q7.question: Why can lubrication reduce wear between moving parts?

answers.a3: It makes all parts the same size

motorbike-s9q1.question: A supply box holds 24 items. Six are used. What fraction remains?

answers.a3: One third

motorbike-s9q2.question: A task begins at 14:35 and lasts 50 minutes. When does it finish?

motorbike-s9q3.question: Four equal groups share 36 items. How many items are in each group?

motorbike-s9q4.question: A reading rises from 40 to 50. What is the percentage increase?

motorbike-s9q5.question: A plan uses a scale of 1 cm to 2 m. What distance does 6 cm represent?

motorbike-s9q6.question: Three loads weigh 12 kg, 15 kg and 18 kg. What is their total mass?

answers.a3: 48 kg

motorbike-s9q7.question: A checklist has 20 items. Four remain unchecked. What percentage is complete?

motorbike-s10q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Check each account against other reliable information
answers.a2: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a3: Choose the more confident speaker automatically

motorbike-s10q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a2: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a3: The person left because they were guilty
answers.a4: The person left the room at 14:10

motorbike-s10q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a3: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion

motorbike-s10q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a1: Proof that the claim is accurate
answers.a3: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations
answers.a4: Proof that no further checking is needed

motorbike-s10q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a2: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor
answers.a3: Mira must be an authorised visitor
answers.a4: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor

motorbike-s10q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a2: Treat your first idea as unchangeable
answers.a3: Change the fact to fit the explanation

motorbike-s10q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a2: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a3: No; earlier events can never cause later ones
